<description>
This is a simple mempool PR that fixes #33510.

Evicting mempool transactions by age (`-mempoolexpiry`, default two weeks) is
incentive-incompatible: it may drop transactions that could still be mined
As discussed IRL and in #33510, this PR hence removes age-based eviction entirely.

Transactions now leave the mempool only via size limiting (`-maxmempool`),
replacement, conflicts, or inclusion in a block. The `EXPIRY` removal reason is
dropped. `-mempoolexpiry` is retained as a hidden no-op that warns when set, so
existing configurations keep starting.

Nice side effects:
- With expiry gone, the `entry_time` index has no readers. Removing it saves an
  ordered-tree node per mempool entry and drops a now unused Boost
  include.
- The `DynamicMemoryUsage()` per-entry estimate drops from three indexes to
  two, so within the same `-maxmempool` budget the mempool fits slightly more
  transactions.
</description>

[2026-10-25] c:6394943202 comment by fametrano (contributor):
Two things look unfinished: the memory estimate still counts three indexes, and `wallet_resendwallettransactions.py` no longer checks that a parent is resubmitted before its child.

tumutech's inline question on the first is still open. `getmempoolinfo` reports `usage` 1192 for one transaction on both 649bc0a (base) and 1556184 (head), since `DynamicMemoryUsage()` still counts 9 pointers per entry. The old resend test expired a parent and child and needed both resubmitted, which works only in insertion order. With that order reversed, base's test fails (`resubmit 1`) and head's passes.

Could this PR use 6 pointers, as tumutech suggests, or drop the "fits slightly more transactions" sentence? For the test, restarting with `-persistmempool=0` and checking that both transactions are back would make the order matter again, since the wallet resubmits them on load.

The rest matches the release note. I measured it with a functional-test script on regtest with mocktime, and the touched functional tests and the unit suite pass on head on macOS (the USDT test skipped). Head keeps transactions past 336 h, loads older `mempool.dat` entries with their entry time, and warns that `-mempoolexpiry` has no effect. One change may deserve a line in the note: `abandontransaction` on a wallet transaction older than two weeks now fails with "Transaction not eligible for abandonment". On base it worked after expiry, until the wallet's next resubmission, within 36 h, put it back. I can share the script as a gist.
</new_statements>
